description.p: Perch is a persistent, compositor-aware window geometry manager. It lives in the system tray, remembers where each window belongs, and restores position, size, monitor, and virtual desktop when a window reopens.

ul.li: Per-window geometry memory across sessions
Snap presets and named layouts
Rules engine for matching windows by class, title, or role
Per-monitor profiles that reconcile on hotplug
Native backends for X11 and KWin/Plasma Wayland; community stubs for Mutter, Sway, and Hyprland

description.p: Windows go back where you left them.

ul.li: The Flatpak is now a download on the release page, as io.github.milnet01.Perch.flatpak. Perch is not on Flathub, which no longer accepts new AI-written applications.

A KDE runtime update no longer breaks the Flatpak. It builds on the freedesktop runtime and carries its own Qt 6.12, and its dialogs use Qt's Fusion style instead of Breeze. They still follow the desktop's light or dark colour scheme.

Perch starts again after it crashes or is killed. The Flatpak used to refuse with "Perch is already running" until you logged out. The single-copy lock is now released by the system the moment Perch stops.
Perch stays connected when KWin reloads its settings. Before, each reload switched window tracking off without a word until Perch was restarted.
A reopened window goes back where you left it. On Plasma Wayland, KWin often moved a just-restored window back to its own spot. Perch now puts it back if that happens in the first half second.

Menus and dialogs are left alone. Perch remembered one position per app and put every window of that app there, so tray menus opened far from the click and dialogs opened at title-bar size. It now never moves menus or splash screens, and remembers and restores only an app's main window.
Quit always quits. Sometimes Perch kept running, invisible, after you quit it or logged out. It now exits within ten seconds whatever happens.

Pixel positions in a rule now count from the monitor it names: x = 120 on HDMI-1 is 120 px in from that monitor's usable left edge. A rule that used whole-desktop pixels for a second monitor needs its x and y reduced by that monitor's position.

A rule that only names a monitor now moves its window there, at the same spot and shrunk to fit if needed, on every backend. Before, X11 put the window off-screen and the config loader refused the rule.
The AppImage starts at login when Start at login is on.
The settings window's tables no longer cut their text off.
Switching tabs no longer snaps a moved window back to its rule.

description.p: Settings that apply at once, a way into settings without the tray, and a broad round of reliability and security fixes.

ul.li: perch --settings opens the settings window even when the tray icon is hidden, such as on GNOME without the AppIndicator extension.
Saving your settings takes effect immediately, with no restart. Windows already placed stay where they are.
On KDE, Perch now hears when you move or resize a window, and reconnects after KWin restarts.
Starting Perch twice no longer runs two copies that fight over your windows.
Perch forgets apps you have not used for 90 days.
Many fixes to how config.toml and state.json are read, saved and recovered, and to window placement on X11, KDE, GNOME and Hyprland.
Security hardening: a badly written title rule can no longer freeze Perch, and config and state directories are created owner-only.

description.p: Onboarding, a single-file download, and a Flatpak that works properly on Plasma Wayland.

ul.li: A first-run setup wizard opens on first launch: it explains that no configuration is needed, checks tray visibility and start-at-login, and names the compositor it detected. It can be reopened from Settings.
Perch now ships as a self-contained AppImage — one file to download and run, with no Python or Qt to install.
An openSUSE and Fedora RPM repository is live, with copy-paste zypper and dnf commands in the README.
The tray menu gains a Donate submenu and a Report an issue entry.
Under Flatpak the tray icon now appears, its menu resolves icons correctly, the KWin script reaches KWin, and start-at-login reaches the Background portal instead of raising.
Tray "Pause restore" is now "Pause Perch", a full panic switch.

description.p: First stable release. Perch remembers where each window belongs and restores geometry (position, size, monitor, virtual desktop) when a window reopens.

ul.li: Full backends for X11 and KWin / Plasma Wayland; community stubs for Mutter, Sway, and Hyprland.
Rules engine with match patterns, named layouts, per-monitor profiles, and exclusions.
Tray icon + PySide6 config dialog with dark-theme support, keyboard navigation, and accessibility labels.
Global hotkeys via the xdg-desktop-portal GlobalShortcuts interface, with KGlobalAccel and XGrabKey fallbacks.
Packaging for Flathub, openSUSE OBS, Fedora COPR, AUR, and the KDE Store.
